sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface biotinylation confirmed plasma-membrane display of HA-GIPR (PMC3296735); N-terminal SNAP-GIPR showed GIP(1-42)-stimulated receptor trafficking (internalization assay) in INS-1 832/3 cells with endogenous GIPR deleted, demonstrating preserved agonist-driven function (PMC10016038); cell-impermeant SNAP probe specifically labeled SNAPf-GIPR at the plasma membrane of HEK293 cells (PMC13544220)
sites.rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1–21 (cleavage after Q21); the mature extracellular N-terminal domain begins at R22 and extends to R136, well clear of TM1 (137–158). Inserting a short tag after residue 21 places it at the very start of the extracellular face, ≥115 residues from the nearest TM boundary. Python verification confirms residue 21 = Q and residue 22 = R in the canonical sequence. Three independent papers pin tags to this exact junction using the phrase 'directly/immediately downstream of the signal peptide' (PMC3296735: HA; PMC4156404: myc; PMC13544220: SNAPf). A fourth paper (PMC10016038) demonstrates that an N-terminal SNAP-tagged GIPR retains GIP-stimulated trafficking, providing functional validation at this topological position. All C-terminal tags in the ledger (V5, eYFP, SYFP2, YFP, Flag, EGFP, SmBiT) land in the intracellular C-tail (residues 396–466) and are excluded. Ledger lines with unstated tag positions (PMC10576055, PMC12771327, PMC7526454 3X-HA, PMC13485621 FLAG+mNG) cannot pin insert_after_residue and were not used as primary evidence. HA epitope (YPYDVPDYA) inserted by overlapping PCR mutagenesis directly downstream of the GIPR signal peptide cleavage site (after residue 21, Q; before residue 22, R) in full-length membrane-anchored human GIPR; surface expression confirmed by surface biotinylation (PMC3296735). A myc-tag was independently introduced at the identical junction ('immediately downstream of the predicted signal peptide') in full-length GIPR for extracellular surface labeling in HEK-293 cells (PMC4156404). N-terminal SNAP-tagged full-length human GIPR (N-terminal tag, same topological position) was expressed in INS-1 832/3 beta cells with endogenous receptor deleted and showed GIP(1-42)-stimulated receptor trafficking, confirming functional surface display (PMC10016038). SNAPf-tagged GIPR (endogenous SP replaced by SNAPf + upstream SP, placing SNAPf at the extracellular N-terminus) was surface-labeled with a cell-impermeant SNAP probe in HEK293 cells (PMC13544220). Additional N-terminal tags (3X-HA, FLAG+mNeonGreen, N-terminal SNAP from Cisbio) reported in PMC7526454 and PMC13485621 are consistent with this position but do not state the exact residue. literature_notes: Only one extracellular site is supported by the ledger. Every ledger line was evaluated: (1) C-terminal tags (V5 PMC3296735, eYFP/SYFP2 PMC7438548, YFP PMC4156404, Flag PMC10842860, EGFP PMC7526454, SmBiT PMC13544220) all land in the intracellular C-tail (topology 396–466) and are disqualified for extracellular tagging. (2) PMC10576055 (Flag/HA by site-directed mutagenesis) and PMC12771327 (HiBiT extracellular detection) do not state the insertion residue and cannot pin insert_after_residue. (3) PMC7526454 (3X-HA N-terminal) and PMC13485621 (FLAG+mNeonGreen N-terminal) state 'N-terminal' without specifying the exact residue; they are consistent with site 1 but were not used as primary evidence. The single qualifying site—after residue 21, the signal-peptide cleavage point—is supported by three papers with explicit positional language and a fourth with functional confirmation.
